notable_absence.finding: This page names classic RBAC roles (Full Admin, Eventing Full Admin) but no Capella project role anywhere - consistent with the batch-wide pattern. Also notable: the REST endpoints are explicitly caveated as supported only 'as long as the content of the Eventing Function body is not created or modified externally (as the internal format of the body is not yet standardized)' - a stability disclaimer on a documented, curl-able public endpoint that doesn't appear elsewhere in this batch.

cross_product_finding: The Capella twin (cloud/eventing/eventing-statistics.md) documents a FOURTH per-Function Deployment Statistic, 'backlog' ('displays the number of mutations waiting to be processed by the function'), that this Server 8.0 page does not have at all - the Server page's own list is exactly three values (success/failure/timeout), stated twice (as counts and as rate charts). This is a genuine content difference, not an extraction gap: the two pages' prose is independently written (the Capella page opens 'Via the Capella UI Eventing Tab' with its own wording for each statistic, not shared text with the Server page, unlike most other pages in this batch which were byte-identical). More strikingly, the Capella page has NO REST API section, NO Dashboard section, and NO curl-to-localhost:8096 examples at all - it stops after the UI statistics and a Log button. Read together with this batch's eventing-memory-quota.json finding (Capella's eventing-faq.md DOES expose a user-configurable memory quota knob), a consistent shape emerges: Capella exposes CONFIGURATION and UI-level observability to users, but does not expose raw per-node REST access or Dashboard-level cluster aggregation the way Server's on-premise Web Console does - a genuinely structural difference driven by Capella hiding individual node topology from the user, not a documentation omission.
